title: Remote Bookkeeper (UK Accounting Firm)
description:
We are SBX Accountants, a fast-growing UK-based accountancy practice working with small businesses, mostly Limited Companies and Sole Traders. We are expanding our delivery team and are looking for an experienced remote bookkeeper to support our client work.



This is a long-term role for the right person.



The role

This position is for a highly-skilled bookkeeper, with occasional administrative and ad-hoc support tasks as required. You will work closely with a UK Chartered Accountant and be part of a growing, process-driven firm.

You must be qualified in bookkeeping and have experience working with UK clients.



Responsibilities

• Day-to-day bookkeeping for UK limited companies and sole traders

• Bank reconciliations and ledger maintenance

• Reviewing transactions

• Correct VAT treatment of transactions at bookkeeping level

• Identifying and flagging potential VAT or coding issues for review

• Assistance in preparing for the year-end accounts, including posting journals/accounting adjustments where needed

• Excel-based tasks and data organisation

• General administrative and ad-hoc support tasks related to bookkeeping and internal firm processes



Key requirements (essential)

• Proven experience in UK bookkeeping

• Qualified bookkeeper (or equivalent professional qualification)

• Several years’ hands-on bookkeeping experience

• Strong working knowledge of QuickBooks and Xero (both required)

• Fluent spoken and written English

• Experience working remotely

• High attention to detail and accuracy

• Proactive, reliable, and able to manage work independently

• Comfortable following processes and implementing feedback



All work is reviewed and supervised - you are not client-facing.



Skills & attributes

• Excellent organisational skills

• Strong attention to detail

• Ability to follow instructions and learn from feedback

• Understanding of confidentiality and data protection requirements

• Comfortable working with cloud-based accounting systems

• Reliable internet connection and home working setup

• Desire to work with a growing UK accountancy practice and take on a greater level of workload and responsibility over the coming months.



Working hours

• 20 hours per week expected, with likely full time capacity over the coming months

• Hours can be flexible

• Opportunity to increase hours significantly as SBX continues to scale

• Pay will be reviewed as responsibility increases, with progression available for high-quality, reliable work.



How to apply

Please include the following in the first 3 lines of your application:

1. Your bookkeeping qualification

2. Your most relevant UK bookkeeping experience (company, dates)

3. Your availability (hours per week and preferred working times)

4. Your experience with QuickBooks and Xero

5. Your favourite hobby!



Final note

This role is best suited to an experienced bookkeeper, and someone who is willing to get stuck in on admin-tasks when bookkeeping work is light. We are looking to build a long-term working relationship with someone who wants to grow alongside a rapidly expanding UK practice.

title: GoHighLevel Implementation & Client Success Operator
description:
GoHighLevel Implementation & Client Success Operator — Long-Term Growth Role



We are a growing U.S. company that helps residential electricians get found, get trusted, and get hired.



I am looking for one exceptional Philippines-based GoHighLevel operator who can take ownership of new-client technical implementation and grow into client onboarding, operations, and eventually customer success.



This is a real, immediate opening with long-term growth potential.



This role will begin with a paid technical test and client implementation work while our client base grows. My intention is for the right person to grow into a significant part-time and ultimately full-time role and make this their primary professional commitment.



This is NOT a generic VA position.



I want someone who knows GoHighLevel extremely well and can independently configure, troubleshoot, QA, document, and improve sophisticated client systems.



Ideally, you know the technical side of GoHighLevel better than I do.



I want someone I can rely on as the technical authority — not someone waiting for me to explain how every part of GoHighLevel should work.



I am looking for someone who wants to become an important long-term part of the business, not someone looking to complete random tasks or collect another freelance client.



WHAT WE ALREADY HAVE



Our core GoHighLevel system is already built as a snapshot.



It includes:



Client website

Lead capture and routing

Pipelines and forms

SMS/email workflows

Missed-call / instant text-back

Reputation/review-request automation

Conversation AI chatbot

AI voice assistant that answers incoming calls

Other follow-up and client communication automations



You will not be starting from a blank account or designing our entire system from scratch.



Your job is to take our established system, customize it correctly for each new client, test everything thoroughly, identify weaknesses or opportunities for improvement, and help make the system better as we grow.



IMMEDIATE RESPONSIBILITIES



For each new client, your core responsibility will be to own the technical implementation from start to finish, including:



Create and configure the GHL subaccount

Deploy the correct snapshot

Customize the existing website with client branding, services, service areas, phone numbers and business information

Connect and configure domains and DNS when needed

Configure LeadConnector phone/SMS and call forwarding

Prepare and submit U.S. A2P 10DLC registrations

Troubleshoot A2P rejections

Configure and test missed-call / instant text-back

Configure and test review-request automations

Verify forms, calendars, pipelines, notifications and workflows

Verify lead routing and client notifications

Assist with Google Business Profile configuration when needed

Configure and test our Conversation AI chatbot

Configure and test our AI voice/call assistant

Test websites on desktop and mobile

Perform complete end-to-end QA

Fix anything that is not working correctly

Document the completed setup



A client implementation is not complete simply because the snapshot was installed.



I expect you to personally verify that calls, texts, forms, workflows, review requests, AI conversations, lead routing, notifications and the website actually work before handoff.



I want someone who thinks beyond:



“I completed the task.”



and instead asks:



“Does the entire system actually work for the client?”



OUR ONBOARDING PROCESS IS STILL BEING BUILT



Our technical system already exists, but our complete new-client onboarding process is not yet fully documented as an SOP.



Initially, I will personally participate in onboarding and customer success.



One of your early responsibilities will be helping me turn our real-world onboarding process into a clean, repeatable system.



I want someone who can identify exactly what information and access we need from every client, find missing steps and unnecessary friction, create implementation and QA checklists, document exceptions and troubleshooting procedures, and continuously improve the process.



I am looking for someone who brings expertise and judgment to the table.



If you know a better way to configure, automate, test or deploy something, I want you to tell me.



I want the person I hire to eventually know this system so well that I can rely on their technical judgment rather than being the person who has to figure everything out first.



AI & AUTOMATION EXPERIENCE IS IMPORTANT



Our system includes both a GoHighLevel Conversation AI chatbot and an AI voice assistant that answers incoming calls.



Hands-on experience with GoHighLevel Conversation AI and/or Voice AI is strongly preferred.



Relevant experience includes:



AI prompts and instructions

Knowledge bases

Lead qualification

Capturing caller/customer information

Appointment or callback handling

Routing and human handoff

Workflows triggered by AI interactions

Testing AI calls and conversations

Troubleshooting incorrect or unexpected AI responses

Improving prompts and call flows

Monitoring AI performance

Preventing hallucinations or inappropriate responses

Escalating situations appropriately to a human



I want someone who understands that an AI system needs to be configured intelligently, stress-tested, monitored and continually improved.



Experience with additional AI/automation tools such as Vapi, Retell, n8n, Make, Zapier, APIs or webhooks is also valuable.



WHERE THIS ROLE CAN GROW



Initially, I will personally manage client relationships.



However, I want the right person to quickly begin participating in and eventually owning client onboarding.



Over time, I want this person to:



Conduct new-client onboarding calls

Collect everything required to launch a client

Own implementation from onboarding through launch

Maintain and improve SOPs and QA systems

Monitor client accounts for technical problems

Proactively identify issues before clients notice them

Communicate directly with clients

Make routine client-requested changes

Help clients understand and use their system

Monitor and improve AI calls/conversations

Help clients get maximum value from what we provide

Eventually own ongoing client success and retention



The long-term opportunity is to become the person who owns much of what happens after a new client signs up.



I am looking for someone who wants to own a business function, not simply complete assigned tickets.



As our client base grows, I want this role to grow with it and ultimately become the person's primary full-time position.



REQUIRED EXPERIENCE



Please apply only if you already have strong, real-world, hands-on GoHighLevel experience.



I am not looking for someone who recently completed a course and is looking for their first serious GHL opportunity.



Strong candidates should have hands-on experience with many of the following:



GHL subaccounts and snapshots

A2P 10DLC / LeadConnector

Websites and funnels

Workflows and automations

Reputation management / review requests

Missed-call text-back

LC Phone / SMS

Forms and calendars

Pipelines

Domains / DNS

Google Business Profile

Conversation AI

Voice AI

Troubleshooting and QA



Experience with U.S. home-service businesses such as electricians, plumbers, HVAC or roofing is a plus.



Experience with client onboarding, customer success, operations management, RevOps, project management, SOP creation or process improvement is a major plus.



EXCEPTIONAL ENGLISH IS REQUIRED



This role is intended to become highly client-facing.



You must have exceptional spoken and written English and be able to communicate naturally, confidently and professionally with U.S. small-business owners.



You should be comfortable:



Leading Zoom onboarding calls

Speaking naturally without relying on scripts

Building rapport

Asking intelligent follow-up questions

Understanding conversational American English

Explaining technical issues in simple language

Handling confused or frustrated clients calmly

Writing clear, professional
s and messages

Representing our company professionally without me being on the call



Exceptional English communication is mandatory.



Technical ability alone is not enough for this position.



THE PERSON I WANT



I value:



Ownership

Excellent judgment

Deep technical competence

Attention to detail

Reliability

Problem-solving

Proactive thinking

Strong documentation

Exceptional communication

Ability to work independently

Curiosity and continuous improvement

Genuine care about client outcomes



If you discover a problem, I don't want you to simply tell me there is a problem.



I want your instinct to be:



Investigate it → understand it → fix it if possible → test the fix → document what happened → tell me what you did.



And if you see something that could be done better, I expect you to speak up.



IMPORTANT: INDIVIDUAL ROLE / NO SUBCONTRACTING



I am hiring one individual, not an agency.



You must personally perform the work assigned to you.



Do not give our passwords, client information, account access or work to friends, coworkers, agencies or subcontractors without my explicit written permission.



If you encounter something you do not know how to do, be transparent about it.



Asking a question is fine.



Giving an unapproved person access to our systems or client accounts is not.



COMPENSATION & GROWTH



The first technical implementation will be a paid $50 USD test project using our standardized system.



For ongoing standardized client implementations, the current target is $50 per completed client setup.



The initial workload will be lighter while our client base grows.



As responsibilities expand into onboarding calls, AI management, SOP/process ownership, operations and client success, responsibility and compensation will increase accordingly.



The right person can grow into a significant recurring role and ultimately a full-time position as our client base expands.



Quality, ownership, communication and long-term fit matter more to me than finding the lowest-cost applicant.



We are hiring now and will move quickly once we find the right person.



HOW TO APPLY



Please do NOT send me a generic cover letter.



Start your application with:



“I personally perform my GHL work.”



Then answer:



How long have you personally worked inside GoHighLevel, and what types of businesses/accounts have you worked on?

Tell me about the most recent U.S. A2P 10DLC registration you personally completed. Have you handled a rejection? What caused it and how did you resolve it?

Have you personally deployed snapshots into client subaccounts? What do you check after deployment before considering an account ready?

Have you configured review-request workflows and missed-call text-back? What do you test before launch?

Have you built or customized websites/funnels inside GHL?

Have you personally worked with GHL Conversation AI or Voice AI? Explain what you built, what the AI was responsible for, and how you tested it.

Have you conducted onboarding calls or communicated directly with U.S. clients? Describe that experience.

Tell me about one SOP, QA system or business process you personally created or significantly improved.

Tell me about a technical or operational problem you discovered before the client noticed it. What did you do?

Are you currently working for another employer or clients? If yes, approximately how many hours per week?

Do you currently own, operate or work for an agency? If yes, please explain.

If this role grows into full-time work, are you willing to make Automatic For You your primary professional commitment?

What type of role would you ideally like to have two years from now?

VIDEO REQUIRED



Please also send a 3–5 minute Loom video with your camera on.



In the video:



Introduce yourself

Explain one GoHighLevel system you personally built or managed

Explain one difficult technical problem you personally solved

Briefly describe any Conversation AI or Voice AI work you've done

Tell me why this particular long-term role interests you



Do not read from a script.



Speak naturally as if you were explaining something to one of our electrician clients.



I will evaluate both your technical experience and your spoken English/client communication ability.



Do not reveal another client's confidential information in your application or video.



If you are excellent at GoHighLevel, strong with automation and AI, communicate exceptionally well, think like an operator, and want to become a trusted long-term part of a growing company, I especially want to hear from you.

title: E-commerce Operations & Customer Support Specialist
description:
About us

We are an Australian online retailer of commercial kitchen equipment, We carry around 49 brands and more than 2,000 products on Shopify — cooking equipment, refrigeration, warewashing, benching and fit-out gear — and sell to restaurants, cafes, hotels, caterers and kitchen fit-out contractors across Australia.

We run from a Sydney head office and showroom, with partner warehouses in Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth. Our promise to customers is simple: the widest range at a guaranteed lowest price, backed by real local support.

We are a small, fast-moving team. You will work directly with the business owner, not through layers of management.

The role

You will be the operational backbone of the store: the person who makes sure every order moves from checkout to delivery cleanly, that every customer gets a fast, clear answer, and that the Shopify catalogue stays accurate.

This is not a call-centre or scripted-chat role. Commercial customers ask real questions about specifications, freight, lead times and warranty, and they expect competent written answers. You will learn our products, our suppliers and our freight process, and become the person the owner trusts to run the day-to-day.

About 60% of the work is logistics and order operations, 30% is customer and sales support, and 10% is Shopify catalogue and admin.

What you will do

Order and logistics operations

Process daily Shopify orders: confirm stock with our warehouses and suppliers, raise purchase orders, and book freight.

Coordinate deliveries of large, heavy commercial equipment: tailgate and forklift requirements, delivery windows, site access, and regional consignments.

Track every open shipment and proactively update customers before they have to ask.

Handle delivery exceptions: delays, damaged freight, missed deliveries, re-deliveries and returns. Own each case through to resolution.

Keep supplier lead times and stock positions up to date so the sales team quotes accurately.

Maintain a clean order pipeline: no order sits without a status, a next action and an owner.

Customer and sales support

Answer customer
s and web enquiries within agreed response times, in clear, professional Australian business English.

Respond to pre-sale questions on products, specifications, compatibility, lead times and freight costs, using supplier spec sheets and our product pages as your source of truth.

Prepare quotes for multi-item and trade orders and follow up on open quotes.

Coordinate warranty and after-sales claims between the customer and the manufacturer's service network.

Escalate pricing decisions, disputes and anything you are not sure about to the owner, with a clear summary and a recommended action.

Shopify catalogue and admin

Update product data: pricing, stock status, lead-time notes, specifications and images, working from supplier information.

Spot and fix catalogue errors (wrong specs, missing images, broken variants) as you find them.

Keep the shared inbox, order notes and internal trackers tidy so anyone can pick up where you left off.

Produce a short daily end-of-day report: orders processed, shipments booked, open issues and what needs the owner's decision.

What we need from you

Must-haves

2+ years in e-commerce operations, order fulfilment, logistics coordination or customer support for an online store.

Hands-on Shopify admin experience: orders, fulfilment, products, variants and inventory. Not just theory.

Excellent written English. You will write to Australian business customers every day and your
s must be clear, warm and correct the first time.

Confident, direct communicator who asks questions early rather than guessing.

Fast learner who is comfortable with technical products. You do not need to know commercial kitchens today, but you must be able to read a spec sheet and explain it plainly.

Highly organised. You track many open items at once and nothing gets dropped.

Able to work Sydney business hours from a quiet home office with a reliable computer, stable internet (25 Mbps+) and a backup connection or power plan.

Nice-to-haves

Experience with Australian freight: booking through carriers or freight forwarders, understanding tailgate delivery, pallets and regional surcharges.

Experience selling or supporting B2B, trade or high-ticket products (equipment, machinery, furniture, appliances).

Familiarity with Google Workspace, Slack, ClickUp and shared inbox workflows.

Basic Xero or invoicing experience.

Experience communicating with Chinese or overseas suppliers on stock and lead times.

Working arrangements

Full-time, 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday on Sydney time. Australian public holidays are observed.

Remote from home in the Philippines. You supply your own computer and internet; we cover work software.

Paid twice monthly via Wise or a payroll platform. 13th-month pay included. Paid leave after a 3-month probation period.

Long-term role. We are hiring someone to grow with the business, not to fill a short project.

Regular pay reviews tied to performance and responsibility.

How to apply

Reply with the following. Applications that skip any item will not be considered.

Your CV and your OnlineJobs.ph profile link, including your English and DISC test results.

A screenshot of the Shopify orders screen from a store you have actually managed, with the store name blurred out.

Your expected monthly salary and earliest start date.

Written answers to these three questions:

Q1. A customer's freight is now five days late and the carrier has no update. Write the
 you would send to the customer.

Q2. A customer asks whether a 900mm-wide gas cooktop will work in their kitchen. What questions do you ask before you answer, and where do you find the answer?

Q3. Describe a time you handled many open orders or tickets at once. How did you keep track and what did you do when something went wrong?



Start your application with the word BENCHTOP so we know you read the full post.

title: Python / Supabase Developer – Data Collection & API Automation
description:
We are looking for a reliable developer to build a small pilot data-automation project for our software company.



The initial project involves collecting newly filed business-registration records from Harris County, Texas, storing and organizing that information in Supabase, and then sending the records to a third-party skip-trace/data-enrichment service.



If the pilot works well, there will be substantial additional work expanding the system to other counties and data sources.



Current Data



The county provides records similar to:



File Number

DBA Name

Address

City

State

ZIP



Example:



B703034

FF ROOFING

5103 HARBOR PALM

RICHMOND

TX

77469



What We Need Built



The developer will:



* Automatically collect/import new Harris County DBA/Assumed Name records

* Store the original records in Supabase/PostgreSQL

* Normalize and clean the data

* Prevent duplicate records from being processed multiple times

* Send addresses to a third-party reverse-address skip-trace/enrichment provider

* Receive and store the enrichment response

* Extract useful contact information such as mobile phone numbers and
s

* Maintain a clean, usable lead record separate from the raw data

* Prepare the resulting records for later CRM/API integration

* Add basic processing/error logging



The skip-trace service may return a very large number of fields. We do not want hundreds of fields imported into our CRM.



We primarily care about extracting useful information such as:



* Contact/person name when available

* Primary mobile phone

* Secondary mobile phone when useful

*
 address

* Phone type

* Verification/confidence information

* Last-seen/recency information

* Match status



The complete raw enrichment response can be retained separately.



Important



This is a pilot project, not a statewide system.



We want to prove Harris County first.



The architecture should, however, be designed so that if the pilot works, we can later add additional counties without rebuilding the entire system.



Conceptually:



County Data

     ↓

Collector / Importer

     ↓

Supabase

     ↓

Normalization + Deduplication

     ↓

Skip Trace / Enrichment API

     ↓

Clean Contact Record

     ↓

CRM / Outreach



Skills We Are Looking For



Strong experience with some or all of the following:



* Python

* Supabase

* PostgreSQL

* REST APIs

* API integrations

* Web scraping / data collection

* ETL / data processing

* Data normalization

* Deduplication

* Scheduled jobs / cron

* JSON

* Webhooks



Experience with lead-enrichment or skip-trace APIs is a plus.



Initial Deliverable



For the first project, we want to successfully process approximately 100–500 Harris County business records through the complete pipeline.



We should be able to see:



* Records collected

* Unique records

* Records sent for enrichment

* Successful enrichment results

* Mobile numbers found

*
s found

* Failed records/errors



If the pilot is successful, the next phase will include additional Texas counties, CRM integrations and further automation.



When Applying



Please answer these questions in your application:



1. How many years have you worked with Python or Node.js?

2. Have you worked with Supabase/PostgreSQL? Please describe.

3. Have you built web scrapers, ETL pipelines or automated data collectors?

4. Have you integrated third-party APIs before?

5. Have you worked with skip-tracing, lead enrichment, people-search or similar data APIs?

6. How would you prevent duplicate records from being processed?

7. How would you structure this so additional counties can be added later?

8. Approximately how long would you expect the Harris County pilot to take?



Please include links or brief descriptions of similar projects you have completed.



Important Application Instruction



Start your application with the words:



HARRIS COUNTY



Applications that do not begin with those words will not be reviewed.



Employment Type



Project-based initially, with strong potential for ongoing work.



We are building a larger software and automation platform, so a successful developer could have significant additional work after this pilot.



⸻

title: AI Docket & Intake Specialist (Litigation)
description:
The short version

You will own the inbox for a three-attorney litigation firm running roughly 75 active matters in state court, federal court, and FINRA arbitration. Every court notice, e-service, piece of mail, and portal filing comes to you first. Your job is to get it logged, filed, and calendared within hours, using an AI system that does the extraction and drafting, and to be the human who confirms the AI got it right before anything is accepted.

This is not a data-entry job with an AI bolted on. The AI does the typing. You do the checking. If a deadline is wrong, it is wrong because a human accepted it, and that human is you. We are hiring for someone who finds that responsibility motivating rather than frightening.



What you'll actually do

Intake, same day. Monitor e-service, court portals (Orange County, Los Angeles, federal PACER, FINRA DR Portal), firm
, and physical mail. Every inbound item is logged against its matter within four business hours of arrival. Not by end of day. Not tomorrow.

Run the log-item workflow. Using Claude Cowork and our firm plugin, run each item through the "log item" skill. The skill files the document to the matter folder, extracts dates and parties, drafts the calendar entries and any deadline the document triggers under the CCP, local rules, or the FINRA Code, and updates the matter's chronology.

Verify before accepting. Open the document. Read what the AI extracted. Confirm the dates, the parties, the deadline rule cited, and the matter assignment against the source. Correct what's wrong. Only then mark the item accepted and let the calendar entries post. This is the core of the job and the part we will train you on most carefully.

Keep the record clean. Every matter has a record: caption, case number, forum, judge or panel, stage, next deadline, next action, owner, last touch. You keep it current. If it isn't in the system, it didn't happen.

Flag what needs a lawyer. The system routes deadline-triggering items and escalations to the responsible attorney automatically. You make sure nothing slips past the routing, and you tell an attorney directly when something looks urgent or unusual.

Improve the system. When the AI extracts something wrong twice, you tell us why. You'll help refine the skills and checklists so the same mistake doesn't recur. Over time you become the person who knows the docketing system best.

Who does well here

You are the person who notices the date on page 4 doesn't match the date on page 1.

You are comfortable reading a court order, a proof of service, or a FINRA scheduling order and understanding what it requires and by when.

You like AI tools and are unbothered by using them all day, but you don't trust them. You verify.

You can hold a checklist and follow it every time, including on the fiftieth item of the day.

You are calm when the inbox is full and honest when you've made a mistake.



Requirements

Two or more years in a litigation docketing, legal assistant, paralegal, or court clerk role, or a paralegal certificate with demonstrable attention to detail.

Working familiarity with California civil procedure deadlines (CCP §§ 1005, 1013, court-day counting) or the ability to learn them quickly with our training.

Experience with e-filing and e-service platforms (One Legal, File & ServeXpress, PACER, or similar).

Proficiency with Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, calendar systems, and document management.

Hands-on experience with Claude, Cowork, or comparable AI assistants for real work, not just experimentation.



Nice to have

FINRA Dispute Resolution experience, including the DR Portal and the Code of Arbitration Procedure.

Experience with a practice-management platform (Clio, Filevine, MyCase).

Prior responsibility for a firm's master calendar.

Experience writing checklists, procedures, or AI prompts for other people to follow.



How we'll measure success

Time from arrival to logged: under four business hours, consistently.

Extraction accuracy on verification: measured monthly, target above 99% after training.

Calendar accuracy: zero missed or misdated deadlines. This is the number that matters.

Silent matters (no logged activity in 30 days): none that you didn't already flag.

title: Content & Growth Manager — Social Media, Community and Lead Generation
description:
We are looking for an experienced Content & Growth Manager to run the day-to-day content, social-media, community-engagement and lead-management system for three established businesses in British Columbia, Canada.

The businesses operate in separate markets:

        1. A Victoria-area real-estate business serving homeowners, buyers, sellers, relocators, upsizers and downsizers.

        2. A custom-home and major-renovation company serving homeowners, landowners, architects, REALTORS and developers.

        3. A civil excavation company building relationships with developers, estimators, general contractors and other industry partners.

These are three separate brands. They must maintain distinct audiences, voices, graphics, content calendars, folders and public identities. This is not a cross-promotion role.

You will not be expected to film and edit every piece of content yourself. You will coordinate with an owner, director, videographer and editor. Your job is to make the complete marketing system work: research, planning, briefing, coordination, writing, publishing, engagement, lead capture, CRM handoff and performance reporting.

We are not looking for someone who measures success only by how many posts were published. We want someone who understands that content should build trust, start useful conversations and create qualified business opportunities.

What you will own

        ◦ Maintain one master production calendar and three separate brand calendars.

        ◦ Research each audience, local market, competitors, search behaviour and useful content opportunities.

        ◦ Turn the owner's knowledge, opinions, project access and recorded footage into clear content briefs.

        ◦ Coordinate deadlines and deliverables with the director, videographer and editor.

        ◦ Adapt approved content appropriately for
, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and other selected channels.

        ◦ Write strong captions, hooks, titles, descriptions, calls to action,
 copy and basic SEO metadata.

        ◦ Schedule, publish and quality-check all approved content.

        ◦ Manage routine comments, direct messages and community interaction in the correct brand voice.

        ◦ Monitor relevant local and industry conversations and identify appropriate opportunities to engage.

        ◦ Ask initial qualification questions, capture contact information and route genuine leads quickly.

        ◦ Maintain accurate lead source, status, notes and follow-up information in the CRM.

        ◦ Maintain organized content libraries, brand assets, permissions, passwords and reusable templates.

        ◦ Produce concise weekly reporting on completed work, audience response, leads, appointments and lessons.

        ◦ Recommend experiments based on evidence and follow them through to a measurable conclusion.

The three content programs

Capital City Group — Real Estate

The primary audience is homeowners in Victoria and the Capital Regional District who may be upsizing, downsizing, selling or relocating. Additional audiences include buyers, first-time buyers, investors and developers.

Content should emphasize:

        ◦ Local property and market intelligence

        ◦ Moving, selling and buying strategy

        ◦ Victoria-area communities and lifestyle

        ◦ Negotiation and transaction knowledge

        ◦ Construction and property-condition insight

        ◦ Selective personal content that supports trust without turning the brand into a lifestyle account

The brand's service promise is: Choose Experience, Expect Results.

Footprint — Custom Homes and Renovations

The audience includes homeowners, landowners, people searching for land, REALTORS, architects, designers and developers. Typical projects are substantial custom builds and renovations.

Content should emphasize:

        ◦ How homes are actually designed and built

        ◦ Cost, process and transparency

        ◦ Diagnosing construction problems

        ◦ Practical solutions and case studies

        ◦ Design-build and preconstruction decisions

        ◦ Evidence of meticulous, capable execution

Footprint must remain publicly separate from the real-estate brand.

Argus Excavating — Civil Construction

The objective is to strengthen Argus's professional civil-contractor presence, build relationships with estimators, general contractors and developers, increase invitations to tender and generate repeat work.

Content should demonstrate:

        ◦ Capabilities, equipment and crews

        ◦ Civil work and site-servicing knowledge

        ◦ Project planning and problem-solving

        ◦ Safety, professionalism and execution

        ◦ Project progress and completed work

        ◦ Credibility with commercial and development partners

What the owner retains

The owner will provide subject-matter expertise, opinions, access to properties and jobsites, and approval of sensitive material. The owner will also handle qualified sales conversations, estimates, negotiations and closing.

You must flag technical, financial, legal, client-sensitive or reputation-sensitive statements for approval. You will be expected to organize content into efficient approval batches rather than requesting scattered approvals throughout every day.

Required qualifications

        ◦ At least three years of relevant social-media, content-marketing or digital-growth experience

        ◦ Demonstrated responsibility for strategy and execution, not scheduling alone

        ◦ Excellent written and spoken English

        ◦ Experience managing more than one brand, client or audience at the same time

        ◦ Strong content-calendar, project-management and deadline-management skills

        ◦ Experience with community management and professional direct-message communication

        ◦ Experience qualifying leads and maintaining a CRM or equivalent lead-management system

        ◦ Ability to interpret analytics and explain what should change as a result

        ◦ Strong judgment, attention to detail and willingness to take ownership

Helpful but not mandatory

        ◦ Familiarity with Follow Up Boss or another sales CRM

        ◦ Familiarity with
 marketing, local SEO and YouTube optimization

What success looks like

Within 90 days, you will have:

title: Executive Assistant & Marketing Specialist
description:
Company Overview



HR TailorMade (HRTM) is an HR consultancy that serves nonprofits and small businesses that need practical, people-focused HR support. We believe in people first, purpose always, helping organizations build better workplaces where their teams can Work Joyfully and Live Fully.



We are a collaborative team that values warmth, clear communication, dependability, and getting things done without unnecessary corporate jargon.



Job Summary



HR TailorMade is looking for a full-time Executive Assistant: Design & Lead Generation to work closely with our CEO, Dr. Tiffany.



This is a remote, Philippines-based role combining three key areas: executive support, graphic design, and lead generation. The ideal candidate is highly organized, creative, proactive, and comfortable taking ownership of projects rather than waiting for step-by-step instructions.



You will help keep the CEO's day organized, create polished and on-brand materials, and support HRTM's efforts to generate and nurture leads.



Location: Remote – Philippines

Employment Type: Full-Time, Independent Contractor

Schedule: Central Time

Manage the CEO's calendar, inbox, meetings, and scheduling.

Coordinate travel, events, appointments, and other logistics.

Assist with client communication and meeting preparation.

Maintain organized files, documents, and CRM records.

Follow up on meetings, commitments, and action items.

Identify potential issues and proactively recommend solutions.



Graphic Design



Create social media graphics, presentations, flyers, one-pagers, and marketing materials.

Design polished and branded client deliverables.

Create graphics for
 campaigns, websites, sales, and marketing initiatives.

Use Canva and Adobe Creative Suite, including Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign.

Assist with AI-powered video creation and editing.

Ensure designs are consistent with HRTM's brand and ready for professional use.



Lead Generation



Support and manage lead-generation activities for HRTM.

Help identify and recommend strategies for generating qualified leads.

Manage lead and pipeline activity using GoHighLevel, HoneyBook, and SmartSuite.

Follow up with prospects and help move leads toward booked sales calls.

Track results and recommend improvements based on what is working.



Qualifications

Proven experience as an Executive Assistant or in a similar role.

Strong graphic design skills using Canva and Adobe Creative Suite.

Experience with AI-assisted video creation and editing.

Experience with lead generation, preferably for service-based businesses.

Experience supporting a consulting firm, nonprofit, or small business is a plus.

Your day may start by reviewing Dr. Tiffany's inbox and calendar, responding to messages, organizing priorities, and confirming upcoming meetings. title: AI-Fluent Executive Assistant, Part-Time (US Operator, Long-Term)
description:
READ THIS FIRST. Your reply must include ONE specific AI workflow you built or used in the last 30 days. What tool, what task, what result. No AI example, no review. That is the only filter that matters.

THIS IS NOT A DATA ENTRY VA ROLE. You will own four lanes. Own means outcome, not task. If I have to remind you twice, it is not owned.

title: VSL/AI Ads Editor
description:
DTC / dropshipping brand doing ~$50k/month in revenue



Role: Video Editor / AI Video Producer Type:



Read this part first



We are not looking for someone to "make our videos look nice."



We are looking for someone who understands that a video's job is to hold attention and make people buy — and who can build that video end to end, including sourcing or generating every frame of footage inside it.



If you need a folder of assets handed to you before you can start editing, this role isn't for you. If you can take a script and a product and come back with a finished, conversion-ready asset, keep reading.



Who we are



We're a direct response DTC brand currently doing around $200k/month, almost entirely on the back of paid media and creative. Creative is our growth lever. Not the site, not the offer tweaks, not the
 flows — the video.



That means the editor seat is one of the highest-leverage roles in the company. When a video wins here, it wins loudly and you'll see it in the numbers within days.



We're scaling, and we want to stop stitching together freelancers per project. We want one highly skilled person who becomes part of the team, learns our angles and our customer inside out, and gets sharper with every batch we ship.



How this role starts (please read carefully)



This does not begin as a full-time position, and that's deliberate.



We start every editor on a lighter workload — a smaller number of videos per week — for the first stretch. Not because we're testing whether you can hold a job, but because we want to see how you fit: how you take feedback, how you handle a script we hand you, how you communicate when something's unclear, and whether the work holds up once the novelty wears off. It also gives you time to learn our customer, our angles, and what a "winning" video looks like in our account specifically.



From there it scales. As the fit proves out and your creatives start performing, the volume goes up, the pay goes up, and the arrangement moves toward a secure, permanent full-time seat — with a defined monthly retainer rather than per-project work.



To be clear about what we're offering:

Phase 1 — Fit: Lower volume, paid per project or at a smaller retainer. Heavy feedback from us. We're both figuring out if this works.

Phase 2 — Ramp: Volume increases, you take on the VSLs and the AI cartoon projects with less hand-holding, pay increases accordingly.

Phase 3 — In-house: Full-time, secure retainer, you own the creative pipeline and have real input on direction. Room to grow into a creative lead as we bring on more editors.



We're not looking for someone to fill a gap for three months. We're looking for the person who's still here in two years running our creative. The slow start is how we get there without either of us wasting the other's time.



If you need immediate full-time income from day one, this probably isn't the right fit right now — and that's fine, just be upfront about it.



What you'll actually be making

1. Long-form VSLs (Video Sales Letters)

-The core of the role. 2–7+ minute sales videos built off scripts we provide.



You'll be responsible for:

-Pacing the entire video so retention doesn't collapse — pattern interrupts, cuts, zooms, motion, sound design, text emphasis, visual proof

-Sourcing your own b-roll. Stock libraries, licensed footage, UGC-style clips, screen recordings, archival, whatever the script calls for. You find it. You don't ask us to send it. In some cases we will also provide clips and we have a bunch of softwares that you can use to make this process easier aswell.

-Generating AI video to fill the gaps stock can't cover — visualizing mechanisms, metaphors, before/after states, scenarios that don't exist as footage.

-Building the visual language for a section, not just laying clips over a voiceover

-Kinetic text, callouts, subtitles, on-screen proof elements, testimonial treatments

-Sound design and music that carries emotional beats without burying the VO



2. AI cartoon / animated videos (short form AND long form)

-We're producing a growing volume of fully AI-generated animated content — story-driven ads, explainer content, character-led narratives.



You'll take a script and:

-Build a consistent character and world (this is the hard part — character consistency across dozens of shots is a real skill and we'll be testing for it)

-Generate the shots yourself using AI image + video tools

-Handle lip sync, voiceover, and audio

-Cut it into a video that actually flows as a story rather than a slideshow of AI clips

-Deliver in both short form (15–60s, vertical) and long form formats



3. Short form paid ads:

-Hook-first ads for Meta / TikTok. High volume, fast iteration. Multiple hook variants of the same body. You'll be cutting these constantly, and you'll be expected to have opinions about which hooks are worth testing.



What we need you to be good at

Non-negotiable:

-Editing that converts, not just editing that looks good. You understand hooks, retention curves, pattern interrupts, why the first 3 seconds decide everything, and how to build toward a CTA. If you've never thought about a video in terms of watch time or CPA, you're not ready for this seat.

-Sourcing your own footage. Independently. You know where to find good b-roll,

-Generating AI video yourself. Not "willing to learn" — actually doing it now. You know how to prompt, how to iterate when a generation is wrong, how to maintain consistency, and how to upscale and clean up output so it doesn't look like AI slop.

-Strong technical craft — clean cuts, deliberate pacing, proper audio levels, colour that matches across mixed sources, subtitles that don't look like an afterthought.

-Speed. We ship a lot. Quality at volume is the whole game.

-Ownership. You get a script and a brief and come back with a finished asset. You flag problems early. You don't go quiet for four days.



Tools — you should be fluent in most of these or their equivalents:

-Editing: Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, or CapCut.

-AI video: Higgsfield, Veo, Kling, Runway, Sora, Hailuo, Seedance — or whatever you've found works better

-AI image: Midjourney, Flux, Nano Banana, Ideogram

-Voice: ElevenLabs or similar

-Upscaling / cleanup: Topaz, Magnific

-Bonus: Descript, Adobe Podcast, motion graphics templating, basic scripting/automation for batching

-Removing text from video: Vmake



Nice to have:

-You've written or restructured direct response scripts before

-You've worked on offers in health and wellnes niche

-You can take a competitor's winning ad, break down why it works, and build a better version

-You track what's new in AI video weekly because you find it genuinely interesting



Who this is NOT for

-Editors who only work from supplied assets

-People who see AI tools as a threat or a gimmick

-"Cinematic" editors who make beautiful videos that don't sell

-Anyone who needs to be chased for updates

title: Head of Finance
description:
Role Overview

The Head of Finance will lead ProfitGrid’s finance function and serve as a strategic business partner to the CEO and leadership team. This role will be responsible for the company’s financial strategy, planning and analysis, accounting and reporting, cash management, financial controls, compliance, and overall financial health.

The ideal candidate is a commercially minded finance leader who can balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution, build scalable finance processes, and provide data-driven insights that support ProfitGrid’s growth and profitability.

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.

10+ years of progressive experience in finance, with significant experience in a senior finance leadership role.

Strong experience in FP&A, financial planning, accounting, reporting, budgeting, and cash management.

Experience partnering with senior leadership and supporting strategic business decisions.

Strong financial modeling and analytical skills.

Excellent understanding of financial controls, compliance, and risk management.

High level of integrity, attention to detail, and commercial acumen.

Develop and execute ProfitGrid’s overall financial strategy aligned with business objectives.

Provide financial insights, analysis, and recommendations to support business growth and profitability.

Monitor actual performance against budget and forecast and identify key variances.

Develop scenario analyses to support strategic decision-making.



3. Accounting & Financial Reporting

Oversee the company’s accounting and financial reporting functions.

Ensure timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting.

Maintain appropriate accounting policies, processes, and controls.

Work closely with external accountants, auditors, tax advisors, and other financial partners.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and regulatory requirements.



4. Cash Management & Treasury

Oversee cash flow management and liquidity planning.

Monitor working capital and optimize cash utilization.

Develop cash flow forecasts and ensure adequate funding for business operations.

Manage banking relationships and other financial institutions.

Establish appropriate controls around company expenditures and payments.



5. Financial Controls, Risk & Compliance

Establish and strengthen financial policies, processes, and internal controls.

Identify and mitigate financial and operational risks.

Ensure compliance with applicable Philippine tax, statutory, and regulatory requirements.

Support internal and external audits.

Maintain strong governance over financial transactions and company resources.



6. Cost Management & Profitability

Monitor operating expenses and identify opportunities for cost optimization.

Analyze business unit and company-level profitability.

Partner with department heads to improve financial accountability.

Develop frameworks for evaluating the financial impact of business decisions.

Drive initiatives that improve margins and overall financial efficiency.



7. Finance Systems & Process Transformation

Build scalable finance processes and systems that can support ProfitGrid’s growth.

Identify opportunities to automate and streamline finance operations.

Improve the quality, accessibility, and reliability of financial data.

Leverage technology and automation to increase finance efficiency and accuracy.



8. Team Leadership

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing finance team.

Establish clear roles, responsibilities, KPIs, and performance expectations.

Develop the team’s technical and commercial finance capabilities.

Foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, continuous improvement, and business partnership

title: AI Specialist / Full-Stack Developer (Next.js, Supabase, AI agents) for a US Property Management System
description:
We are a short term rental management company in the United States. We run the properties and we rent every one of them on Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia and Vrbo at the same time.



The interesting part is not the properties. It is that we stopped running the company out of other people's software. We wrote our own property management system. It is Next.js and Supabase and Postgres, and it already holds the reservations, the bank feed, the payments, the owner accounting and the channel connections in one place. It is most of a real PMS already. What is left is the part that decides whether the team ever closes the other tabs.



I lead the AI and systems side here and I write most of this code today. I am hiring one person to work next to me on it. Not to be handed tickets. To own parts of it.



I am keeping our name and our product off this post on purpose, and I would rather say that plainly than have you wonder. You will know exactly who we are on the first call. What I can tell you now is the work, and the work is below.



What you will own



- Finishing the staff cockpit. One screen where the team sees today's arrivals, departures, turnovers and the things that are quietly wrong, instead of five screens that each know a third of the answer.

- The owner portal. Property owners log in and see their nights, their earnings and their statements. It is built and nobody has ever used it. Getting it from built to used is a real job with real edge cases.

- Guest messaging. Right now we can read every guest conversation across Airbnb and Booking.com and we can send almost nothing. Outbound messaging, templates that fire on booking and check-in, and a preview mode so nothing goes out by accident.

- Channel manager work. Pushing rates and minimum stays out through the channel manager that fans them to the OTAs, inside a strict API credit budget. Availability writes that can never open a night a feed has already blocked.

- Reconciliation. Matching bookings to payouts to bank rows across four channels and three payment processors. We have an engine that does this well. It needs to keep doing it well as we add channels.

- AI agents and automations that do actual work. Reading OTA statement
s, drafting guest replies for a human to approve, flagging a reservation that will not reconcile before anyone notices. Small, checkable, boring in the best way.



Owning quality on all of the above. Every change you ship leaves behind a check that fails if the change breaks.



The stack you will actually touch



The app is TypeScript on Next.js and React, styled with Tailwind, on Supabase with Postgres underneath. The database is not a thin layer here. A lot of the real logic is in SQL functions and migrations, and you will write both.



The outside world reaches us through a channel manager, which is our one and only write path out to the OTAs, a legacy reservation system we can read but never write to, a bank data provider for the account feeds, and a payment gateway for cards. Deploys run in Docker on a self hosted platform on our own servers, and the build gate runs our own checks before anything goes live.



I would rather hire someone who reads the whole spec than someone who starts typing quickly, so I put something in here to see who gets this far. If you are reading this, begin your answer to the "Why this role" question on the application form with the single word tarsier on a line by itself, then write your real answer underneath.



For the AI layer we use Claude and OpenAI through their APIs, with tool use, plus n8n for the glue that does not deserve its own service. If you have opinions about when an agent is the wrong answer, we will get along.



What I need from you



Two or more years shipping production web apps in TypeScript, on Next.js or Node. Not tutorials, not a bootcamp capstone. Something real people used.



SQL you can defend. Joins, aggregates, window functions if you have them, and a working understanding of why an index matters. Postgres or Supabase specifically is a strong plus.



REST APIs and webhooks, from both sides. You have consumed a paginated, rate-limited third party API and handled it failing halfway through.



Git that you use like an adult. Branches, small commits, a pull request someone else can read.



At least one AI or LLM feature you actually deployed. Prompting, tool use, and some way you knew whether it was working. I will ask what it got wrong and how you found out.



Docker and Linux basics. You can read a Dockerfile, tail a container log, and get around a server over SSH without a tutorial open.



Written English strong enough to disagree with me in writing and be understood the first time.



Full shift overlapping United States Eastern time, described below.



A portfolio or GitHub. This is not optional. If your best work is private, tell me what it did and be ready to walk me through it on a call.



Nice to have, genuinely optional



n8n. Playwright or any real browser automation. Python. Any prior work with a property management system or a channel manager, whichever brand it was. Cloudflare. Any self hosted deploy platform. Accounting or reconciliation exposure of any kind, even from a bookkeeping job, because half of this system is money.



What junior, mid and senior look like in this seat



I am writing this out so you can place yourself instead of guessing.



Junior here means you have shipped one or two real apps, you can read a Next.js codebase you did not write and add a page to it, you have written SQL joins but never tuned a query, and you have called an LLM API once or twice. You would work on one clearly scoped screen at a time and I would review your work closely. That is a fine place to start. Expect the bottom of the range.



Mid means two to four years of shipping, and you can own a feature from the migration to the deployed screen without me holding the other end. You write the check that proves your change works before I ask for it. You have put an LLM feature in front of real users and you remember exactly how it embarrassed you. This is the level I am hiring for.



Senior means you have owned a data model other people depended on, you can look at a reconciliation engine and tell me where it will drift six months from now, and you push back on scope and are sometimes right. Top of the range, and I will go above it for the right person.



If you are between two of these, apply as the lower one and let the work say otherwise.



How we work



Small changes, shipped often. Nothing sits in a branch for three weeks.



Every change that has logic in it leaves behind a check. If the logic breaks later, something fails loudly. We do not rely on remembering.



We use Claude Code and agentic tooling daily, and I expect you to. That is not a shortcut here. It means you are responsible for more code than you typed, so you read all of it and you own every line of it. An AI wrote it is not an explanation for a bug in this company.



Money paths stay gated. Anything that can move a dollar is off by default and turns on deliberately, in front of a human. If that sounds slow, it is, and it is not up for debate.



Direct feedback in both directions. I will tell you plainly when something is wrong. Do the same to me.



Async first, in writing. I would rather read four clear sentences from you than sit through a meeting.



Schedule and pay



Full time, forty hours a week, remote, anywhere in the Philippines.



Core overlap is 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM Eastern time, which is roughly 9:00 PM to 5:00 AM in Manila. I am asking for full hours in a day when we can actually talk.



6 to 12 US dollars per hour, depending on where you land in the levels above. Paid twice a month. Thirty day trial at full hours and your full agreed rate, and at the end of it either of us can walk away without a story.



Long term seat. I am not filling a project, and I am not looking for someone to hand off to in six months.



How to apply



Do not send a proposal here with a CV attached and nothing else. I will not open it.



The whole application is one form:







Budget about forty five minutes. Most of that is one small technical task, and it is a real problem out of our system rather than a puzzle I made up. You will need a computer, not a phone.



Here is the order:



Read this post to the end. There is a reason for that sentence.



Open the form and answer it in one sitting. It accepts one response per person and it cannot be edited afterwards, so do not open it until you have time.



Do the technical task honestly. Use whatever tools you use at work, including AI, and then tell me on the form what you used and what you changed by hand. I am not testing whether you use AI. I am testing whether you can tell when it is wrong.



Submit. You get a copy of your answers by
.



Then, and only then, send your proposal here on OnlineJobs.ph with the three short answers below so I can match it to your form.



What happens next: I read every form myself. If your answers hold up, you get a short written exchange first, then a call with me on Zoom, camera on, where we look at your technical task together and I ask you to change something in it live. If that goes well, a small paid trial task before the thirty day trial starts.



If your application is generated end to end by a language model, I will know from the form, and you have wasted your own evening. If you use AI as a tool and think for yourself, you are exactly who I want.



One last thing



I read every application the same week it arrives, and I answer all of them, including the ones I turn down. If you are the person I am describing, you will find the form easy and slightly fun, and you should apply tonight.

READ THIS ENTIRE POST BEFORE APPLYING. There are specific instructions at the bottom, and only complete applications are reviewed.

>> ABOUT XTENDENCY.AI

Written English at a professional level. Spoken English that is clear, with an accent that is easy to understand for the whole team and for clients. We assess both on your video application and on a live call.

title: Shopify Inventory & Merchandising Specialist
description:
Shopify Ecommerce Inventory & Merchandising Specialist



Full-Time | Remote | US$280 per Week



We’re hiring an experienced Shopify Ecommerce Inventory & Merchandising Specialist to support the Australian and New Zealand ecommerce operations of a leading global headwear and lifestyle brand.



This is a long-term, hands-on position focused on:



Ecommerce inventory accuracy

Shopify product management

Inventory and trading reports

Onsite merchandising

Reliable communication and follow-through

You’ll report to the Head of Digital AU & NZ and collaborate with Ecommerce, Planning, Marketing and Operations.



This is not a basic virtual assistant or data-entry position. You’ll be trusted to manage important recurring responsibilities, identify problems early and follow issues through to resolution.



Compensation and schedule



Pay: US$280 per week

Payment frequency: Weekly

Hours: 40 hours per week

Schedule: Monday to Friday, aligned with Australian business hours

Location: Fully remote

Engagement: Full-time, long-term opportunity

The advertised rate is fixed. Please only apply if you are comfortable with the compensation and schedule.



Key responsibilities



Ecommerce inventory



Maintain accurate stock-on-hand information in Shopify.

Assist with inventory reconciliation between Shopify and SAP.

Monitor sell-through, weeks of cover, aged stock, out-of-stocks and overstock risks.

Investigate inventory discrepancies and follow them through to resolution.

Maintain recurring inventory health and exception reports.

Support replenishment and back-in-stock processes.

Communicate inventory risks before they affect customers or create additional work for the team.

Shopify product management



Create, enrich and maintain accurate Shopify product listings.

Manage descriptions, imagery, specifications, tags, metafields and categorisation.

Assign products to the correct collections and merchandising rules.

Maintain accurate filters, navigation and collection structures.

Conduct regular checks for missing, incorrect or outdated product information.

Troubleshoot product-data and website-display issues.

Support new product launches, seasonal changes and promotional activity.

Reporting and analysis



Produce recurring inventory and merchandising reports.

Report on stock on hand, out-of-stocks, aged inventory and sell-through.

Support weekly and monthly ecommerce trading reports.

Identify stock risks, commercial opportunities and data-quality issues.

Turn large product and inventory datasets into clear, practical insights.

Help improve and automate recurring Shopify and SAP reports.

Site merchandising



Manage Shopify collections, product sequencing and collection sorting.

Maintain merchandising logic based on stock availability and trading priorities.

Identify and correct broken collections, incorrect links and miscategorised products.

Support basic website updates when required.

A dedicated local team member manages most content execution, so advanced content-production experience is not required.



Essential experience



You must have:



Strong, hands-on Shopify experience.

Ecommerce inventory, stock-reporting or product-administration experience.

Strong Excel skills and confidence working with large datasets.

Experience creating and enriching ecommerce product listings.

Knowledge of Shopify collections, tags, metafields and product categorisation.

Excellent written and spoken English.

Strong attention to detail and problem-solving ability.

Full-time availability during Australian business hours.

SAP experience



SAP experience is highly regarded but not essential.



Strong Shopify capability is the priority. The successful candidate can be trained in the company’s SAP processes.



Highly regarded



Fashion, apparel, footwear, accessories or lifestyle-brand experience.

Multi-channel inventory-management experience.

Familiarity with Shopify applications and advanced metafields.

Reporting automation, BI or data-visualisation experience.

Experience supporting ecommerce launches and promotions.

The person we want



Skills will get you shortlisted. Your working style will get you hired.



You must be:



A strong and dependable communicator

Efficient and organised

Proactive when identifying problems

Highly detail-oriented

Methodical and consistent

Motivated and accountable

Comfortable taking ownership

Reliable when working remotely

You don’t disappear when something goes wrong. You investigate the issue, communicate clearly and help drive it through to resolution.



What success looks like



Within your first three months, you will:



Establish a reliable inventory-monitoring routine.

Maintain consistently accurate Shopify product information.

Deliver reports correctly and on time.

Proactively communicate stock risks and discrepancies.

Execute product launches and merchandising updates accurately.

Build trust through dependable communication and follow-through.

How to apply



Please provide:



A short summary of your Shopify and ecommerce inventory experience.

An example of an inventory discrepancy you personally identified and resolved.

Details of the Shopify product and merchandising tasks you have managed.

The Excel formulas and tools you regularly use.

Details of any SAP, ERP, fashion or lifestyle-brand experience.

Confirmation that you can work 40 hours per week during Australian business hours.

Confirmation that you accept the fixed rate of US$280 per week.

A link to a 60–90 second video introducing yourself and explaining why you suit the role.

Begin your application with “Shopify Accuracy”.



Applications that ignore these instructions will not be considered.
